title: Projective modules over local rings are free in arbitrary rank
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal. Let $P$ be a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], with no finite-generation hypothesis. Then $P$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]: there are a set $B$ (possibly empty or infinite) and an $R$-linear isomorphism $\bigoplus_{b\in B}R\cong P$.

source.place: Tag 0593, theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring; used in the first sentence of flat.tex, Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-countable-decomposition] to $P$ over the given commutative ring $R$. Obtain an isomorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}P_i\cong P$ in which every $P_i$ is projective and countably generated. Fix $i\in I$; the next two steps prove that $P_i$ is free.

source.place: Tag 0593, theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring; Tag 0590, lemma-projective-free, using Tag 058Y, theorem-projective-direct-sum

proof.text: Consider any decomposition $P_i=N\oplus F$ with $F$ finite free. The complement $N$ is projective by the direct-summand characterization of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]: take split maps $j:P_i\to E$ and $s:E\to P_i$ with $E$ free and $sj=1$, and the inclusion $a:N\to P_i$ and projection $r:P_i\to N$ with $ra=1$. Then $(rs)(ja)=1_N$, so $N$ is a direct summand of the free module $E$. For every $x\in N$, [lem-trf-projective-element-free-summand], applied to the projective $R$-module $N$ over this same local ring, gives a free direct summand $G\subseteq N$ containing $x$. This verifies the complementary-summand hypothesis of the countable freeness criterion for every such decomposition.

source.place: Tag 0593, theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring, applying Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, to complements in Tag 0591

proof.text: The module $P_i$ is countably generated by step 1, and step 2 verifies the hypothesis for every decomposition of $P_i$ with a finite free summand. Hence [lem-trf-countably-generated-freeness-criterion] gives that $P_i$ is free. This holds for every $i\in I$.

For each $i$ choose a basis $(e_{i,b})_{b\in B_i}$ of $P_i$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The vectors $e_{i,b}$ placed in the $i$-th coordinate form a basis of $\bigoplus_iP_i$: each family has finite coordinate support, each of its coordinates has finite basis support, and the union of these finitely many finite supports gives a finite expansion; uniqueness follows by comparing coordinates and then using the uniqueness in each basis. Transport this basis along the isomorphism of step 1. Its index set is $B=\coprod_{i\in I}B_i$, yielding $\bigoplus_{b\in B}R\cong P$. If $I$ is empty this is the empty basis of the zero module, so this case is included.
